//: tsconfig.json has strictNullChecks:false and noImplicitAny:false, with 361
`any` usages across src/. In a system that issues tax invoices that means
the compiler will not tell you a price can be undefined before you multiply
by it — precisely the class of bug that produces a wrong invoice.
Flipping strict on globally would produce hundreds of errors at once and
get switched back off within a day. Instead this config enforces FULL
strict mode on an allowlist, and CI fails if anything on that list
regresses. The list only ever grows.
To add a file: fix it, add it to `files` below, confirm `npm run
typecheck:strict` is clean, commit. The base tsconfig still compiles
everything else, so nothing breaks while the list is short.
Seeded with the money path, because that is where a null bug costs money.
